level_problem: First conditional at A2.2 is a little high but acceptable.
sense_problem: 'would' is a believable mistake (mixing with second conditional). 'What would you do if the shop is closed' is not standard English, so no second answer.

instruction_problem: Open gap: many words fit (never, rarely, seldom, can't, shouldn't, won't, mustn't). Nothing says which kind of word is wanted (negative auxiliary? adverb?). 'one word' makes 'don't' a contraction and rules out 'do not'. Needs a clue or a fixed form. Also 'try not to' etc. are not one word, so ignore them.
level_problem: Fine for B1.1, even easy (simple present negative is A1-A2).
sense_problem: Sentence is natural and logical; 'never/rarely' give a slightly different meaning but are correct.

instruction_problem: The cue (start) is given but not the form wanted. Present simple 'starts' is the intended timetable use, but 'is starting', 'will start', 'is going to start' (and 'is due to start') are also correct English for a future event. Without a note such as 'timetable' or 'use the present simple', several answers are possible. Also does not make clear if 'start' may be changed.
level_problem: Timetable present simple for future is fine for B1.1.
